subtype_label: Focus internal / focus inference (no given focus)
query: What are the main kinds of issues these support tickets are about?

judge.implied_focus: The nature/type of the support issue (what the ticket is about, characterized along category, subtype, affected component, scope, and impact)

per_column.name: issue_category
per_column.rationale: Directly names the kind of issue (bug, outage, feature_request, etc.), which is the core of the query's 'main kinds of issues'.

per_column.name: issue_subtype
per_column.rationale: Refines the category into a finer thematic grouping (auth, billing, UI/UX), adding useful granularity to the same focus.

per_column.name: affected_component
per_column.rationale: Identifies the system area implicated, a coherent facet of what an issue is about.

per_column.name: incident_scope
per_column.rationale: Characterizes breadth of impact (single_user vs tenant); a sensible attribute of an issue though slightly more impact-oriented than kind-oriented.

per_column.name: operational_impact
per_column.rationale: Describes consequence of the issue; supports understanding but leans toward impact rather than 'kind', still coherent with the focus.

judge.rationale: The columns collectively centre on one coherent, data-inferable focus: characterizing the nature of support issues. issue_category, issue_subtype, and affected_component form a clean, differentiated hierarchy of what a ticket is about at a useful granularity, directly answering 'main kinds of issues'. incident_scope and operational_impact extend the focus into consequence/breadth facets; they are coherent and analyst-actionable but drift slightly from 'kind of issue' toward impact, which is why coherence and structure are not perfect. Nothing here is a mechanical restatement or generic noise (no token counts or bare sentiment), and the implied focus is clearly investigable (e.g., which categories dominate, which components drive outages).
